story: Parvati, daughter of the mountain king Himavan, is the rebirth of Sati, Shiva's first wife. To win the grieving ascetic Shiva, she performed years of fierce penance until he accepted her. Together they are the parents of Ganesha and Kartikeya.
belief: Parvati is the gentle form of Shakti, the divine feminine power. Women fast and pray to her for a happy marriage on festivals like Teej, and she is honoured as the mother of the universe.
turns: She made Ganesha from the turmeric paste on her own body to guard her door while she bathed, which led to his clash with Shiva. Her grief and anger then forced Shiva to bring him back to life.
facts: Ardhanarishvara shows Shiva and Parvati as one body, half male and half female.
Durga and Kali are often described as her fierce forms.
Her name comes from parvata, meaning mountain.
lessons: Steady effort can win what force cannot.
Gentleness and fierceness can live in one person.
Love may mean waiting, but never losing yourself.
more: As Gauri she is at the heart of the Gangaur festival in Rajasthan.
Annapurna, the goddess of food and nourishment, is one of her forms.
